correctness.rationale: Use Long–Narayanan eventual period≤2 to reduce initially periodic states to fixed or two-cyclic states. For an initial state with ordered label blocks of multiplicities a_i, under one update each gap becomes old gap−(a_i+a_{i+1}); paired strict comparisons reverse exactly when 1≤d_i≤a_i+a_{i+1}−1, while ties persist. This is necessary and sufficient for F²(x)=x, with only the constant fixed class. Counting label assignments and independent gaps gives the weighted composition census. Append-a-part rank-two transfer matrix sums to EGF (1−e^(−z))/(1−z+z²−ze^z). Its positive simple dominant pole and aperiodic positive matrix imply C_n~κ n!ρ^(−n), ρ≈0.4695449931. Independent direct enumeration of all initially periodic normalized boxes for n=1..4 gave 1,3,19,163; analytically argued block gaps support all n.
residual_risks: Only initially periodic states modulo simultaneous integer shifts, not all transient states or basins.
Finite n≤4 checks cannot establish analytic asymptotics.

value.rationale: An exact all-order count of initially periodic integer diffusion states is a natural dynamical invariant, refining qualitative global eventual periodicity. The weighted-composition classification, two-cycle orbit census, closed EGF and factorial-exponential asymptotic are nontrivial enumerative consequences that future diffusion studies can use.
residual_risks: The fixed-point and eventual period≤2 facts are credited and not treated as original.

limitations: Labelled graph states modulo integer translation only; no count of eventual-entry basins.
Pole uniqueness uses positivity/aperiodicity, not merely numerical root fitting.
